target_customer: Lawyers who want to start and own AI-native law firms
problem: Lawyers who leave large firms must build technology, intake, back office and client acquisition themselves.
business_model: Operating partner for lawyer-owned firms providing software, staff, back office, working capital and client acquisition; fee terms not found

founders.name: Sasha Zyuzin
founders.background_notes: YC page lists Black Hat USA 2025 and SANS OSINT Summit 2025 talks, and leading the UMD cybersecurity club.

founders.name: Jason Guo
education: University of Maryland, computer engineering (in progress)

founders.name: Matthew Pallan
education: University of Maryland, Computer Science and Real Estate
founders.background_notes: Built low-latency trading systems per the YC page.

competitors.name: Moritz
competitors.what: AI-native corporate law firm, 9M seed reported with YC
competitors.traction_then: Hired lawyers from Cooley, Goodwin and Fenwick

competitors.name: Norm Law
competitors.what: AI-native firm targeting Big Law corporate clients

technical_complexity.rationale: Legal workflow software plus intake and operations is standard engineering; the hard parts are professional rules on firm ownership and fee sharing.

defensibility.rationale: Several funded AI-native firms use the same pitch and lawyers own the firms, so lock-in is limited.

market_need_then: Bloomberg Law reported frustrated lawyers leaving Big Law for AI-native firms in 2026, backed by venture capital.

branding.name_origin: Erinys is the Greek name for the Furies, goddesses of vengeance and justice; no source says the company chose it for that reason.

identity.visual_style: Uses a section sign symbol as a motif on the site, unexplained.
identity.voice_and_tone: Lawyer-ownership pitch: 'Welcome to the firm you started.'

brand_strength.rationale: Mythic, legal-sounding name with a legal motif, but no press about the brand found.

outcome_analysis: Erinys is a Summer 2026 company with three University of Maryland founders and security and low-latency engineering backgrounds. No outcome yet. The model competes with better funded AI-native firms and depends on regulatory acceptance of its structure, so early firm signups will be the key signal.
notes: Dealroom lists a 125K seed, a single locked aggregator figure, unverified so no round recorded. Directories describe Erinys differently (plaintiff-side litigation network, False Claims Act software). Founding year not found. The 125K seed rests on a single database (Dealroom, partly locked, no date).
